items.stem: On reaching a collapsed person outdoors, the first action is to:

options.text: Check the scene for danger to yourself and others
options.rationale: Correct: scene safety comes before casualty contact.
Assessment and safety precede any intervention.

options.text: Move the person to a vehicle

items.explanation: Correct: scene safety comes before casualty contact.

items.stem: Which TWO are appropriate for controlling severe external bleeding? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Apply firm direct pressure to the wound
options.rationale: Correct: direct pressure is the first-line control.
Correct: severe bleeding needs emergency help.

options.text: Remove a deeply embedded object to clean the wound
options.rationale: Embedded objects should be stabilised, not removed.

options.text: Give the casualty a hot drink

items.explanation: Correct: direct pressure is the first-line control.

items.stem: An unresponsive adult is breathing normally. The appropriate theory-based action is to:

options.text: Place them in the recovery position and monitor
options.rationale: Correct: protects the airway while help is sought.
CPR is for a casualty not breathing normally.

options.text: Sit them upright against a wall
options.rationale: Does not protect the airway if they deteriorate.

options.text: Leave them supine and walk away

items.explanation: Correct: protects the airway while help is sought.
